name: Kang-Petrov Arms KPR-357 'Journeyman'
description:
The Kang-Petrov KPR-357 is a medium-frame double-action revolver chambered in .357 Magnum, designed as the revolver equivalent of their ubiquitous KP-19 — reliable, affordable, and available everywhere. The frame is carbon steel with a matte stainless finish, and the four-inch barrel is heavy-profile for improved accuracy and reduced muzzle flip. The cylinder also accepts .38 Special ammunition for practice and reduced-recoil applications.

The Journeyman is the revolver that security professionals carry when they prefer wheel guns over semi-automatics. The .357 Magnum round provides stopping power that exceeds 9mm and approaches .44 Magnum at close range, while the weapon's medium frame keeps it manageable for extended carry. The ability to load .38 Special for practice reduces training costs significantly — a practical consideration that Kang-Petrov highlights in their marketing.

Kang-Petrov produces the KPR-357 in the same factories that build the KP-19, applying the same philosophy of volume production and consistent quality. The result is a revolver that lacks the hand-fitted refinement of premium offerings but delivers dependable performance at a price point that working professionals can afford without wincing.
specifications:
caliber: .357 Magnum / .38 Special
effective_range: 45 meters
rate_of_fire: Double-action revolver
magazine_capacity: 6 rounds (cylinder)
weight: 0.96 kg
tactical_use: A versatile duty revolver offering .357 Magnum stopping power with the option of .38 Special for training and reduced-recoil situations. The heavy-profile barrel improves accuracy and reduces muzzle flip. Suitable for open carry by security professionals and personal defense. Reloading is slower than semi-automatics — speedloaders are standard equipment for serious carriers.
cultural_context: The Journeyman is the working person's magnum revolver. It lacks the drama of the Mauler and the prestige of higher-end offerings, but it performs its job without complaint. Among revolver carriers, the KPR-357 is respected as an honest weapon — no flash, no gimmick, just competence.
story_hooks: A Journeyman loaded with .38 Special wadcutters is used in what appears to be a training accident — but the forensics don't match any shooting range in the district.
Kang-Petrov is discontinuing the KPR-357 due to declining revolver sales. The announcement triggers a buying rush among loyalists who consider it the last affordable quality revolver.
physical_description: The KPR-357 is a compact, utilitarian revolver with a brushed stainless steel finish worn dull by years of holster carry and rain exposure. Its four-inch barrel sits heavy and purposeful above the medium carbon-steel frame, the cylinder scarred from repeated loading cycles. The grip is textured black polymer, molded for function over form, with faint wear marks from gloved hands.
